trigger.situation: Python CSV DictReader raises KeyError because the script accesses row['amount'] but the file's header is upper-case (AMOUNT). The same class of bug recurs whenever a CSV pipeline's column names don't match the script's case.

body.mechanism: csv.DictReader keys are case-sensitive. It returns row dicts keyed by the literal header strings, so any case mismatch surfaces as KeyError at the access site.
deadEnds: wrapping the access in try/except is a band-aid that hides every other column typo too
lower-casing every header at read time is invasive and silently breaks downstream consumers that expect original case
body.unlock: match the dict access to the actual header case (e.g. row['AMOUNT'] when the header line is 'ID,AMOUNT'); if you don't control the header, normalise once at the read boundary with an explicit header transformer.
body.verification: rerun the pipeline; KeyError disappears and output.txt contains the expected aggregate.
